foreign-law-research 1.1.0 introduces a comprehensive methodological framework for conducting foreign law research.

- Added detailed step-by-step methodology (Deep Research 8-step method) tailored to major research scenarios (investment, M&A, risk assessment, dispute resolution, etc.).
- Introduced a hierarchical resource library with clear prioritization, including recommended databases, tools, and their usage notes.
- Standardized working directory structure for organizing research outputs and ensuring traceability.
- Emphasized time sensitivity and requirement to cross-verify sources; outlined best practices for fact extraction, report drafting, and source citation.
- Provided template for report structure and key reminders regarding limitations and legal disclaimers.

1. No changes detected; the skill contents remain the same in this release.
2. Documentation, methodology, resources, and workflow remain unchanged.
3. Version increment without modifications in files or functionality.
Fully English description. A Skill for cross-border legal research.

A Claude Code and OpenClaw Skill for researching foreign law questions. When doing cross-border business, one of the hardest tasks is figuring out the legal rules in an unfamiliar jurisdiction. This skill classifies legal sources into four tiers: (1) primary legislation and official interpretations (most authoritative), (2) international guides like Chambers and ICLG (frequently updated, free), (3) law firm articles and commentary (reference only), and (4) AI-generated leads (must be verified manually). Features timeliness sensitivity grading (sanctions/data compliance vs stable contract principles), two research modes (quick overview vs deep dive), and .docx report output with reasoning chains and source attribution. Inspired by wshuyi/deep-research.

Based on the methodology from 《快速检索外国法问题：从中英文资料到AI的全方位指南！》(A Comprehensive Guide to Searching Foreign Law). Features: source authority hierarchy (L1-L4 primary law > international guides > firm commentary > AI leads), timeliness sensitivity grading, two research modes (overview vs deep dive), and .docx report output with reasoning chains. Inspired by wshuyi/deep-research.

A structured 8-step methodology for researching foreign law questions. Features source authority hierarchy (L1-L4), timeliness grading, certainty labels, topic-resource matching, and .docx report output. Covers 13 legal topics across 100+ jurisdictions. Free resources: ICLG, Chambers, Legal500, Lex Mundi, WIPO Lex, EUR-Lex, and more.
